questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A) An earthquake hitting Lahore in Pakistan.
B) Rescue operation after the earthquake.
C) A factory building being damaged in the earthquake.
D) Relief work in the collapsed factory building.

explain.定位:
At least 16 people were killed and up to 150 trapped under the rubble when a factory
collapsed in an industrial area of Lahore in eastern Pakistan. Formerly several stories high, no
part of the building remained standing after the disaster, and hundreds of rescue workers
including soldiers have been picking through concrete and bricks to find survivors. Dozens
have been pulled out alive.
巴基斯坦东部拉合尔一处工业区一座工厂倒塌，至少 16 人遇难、多达 150 人被困瓦砾之
下。该楼原本有数层高，灾后无一处仍然屹立；包括士兵在内的数百名救援人员一直在混凝
土与砖块中翻找幸存者，已有数十人被活着救出。
explain.信号:
全篇主语始终是『倒塌的工厂 + 救援』。判主旨靠『反复回到哪个点』而非单句信号词：开
篇 a factory collapsed 点出工厂倒塌，紧接 hundreds of rescue workers including
soldiers have been picking through concrete and bricks to find survivors 与 Dozens
have been pulled out alive 整段都在讲倒塌建筑里的救援。地震只在末尾作为可能成因被
一句带过，重心始终压在『倒塌工厂的救援』上。
explain.替换:
a factory collapsed ↔ the collapsed factory building
动词 collapsed 改写成形容词 collapsed building，指同一座倒塌的楼
rescue workers including soldiers have been picking through concrete and bricks to find survivors
↔ Relief work
『救援人员翻找幸存者』概括成上位词 Relief work（救灾工作）
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
An earthquake hitting Lahore in Pakistan. 借了录音里真出现过的 earthquake 和
Lahore in eastern Pakistan，听着耳熟。但地震只在末尾 may have suffered damage in
last week's earthquake 作为可能成因被一句带过，全篇主体是工厂救援，把背景当主旨即
以偏概全。
借用原文：may have suffered damage in last week's earthquake that hit Afghanistan and Pakistan
B) 偷换概念
Rescue operation after the earthquake. 抓住了录音里的 rescue operation，救援确实是
重心之一。但它把救援系在 earthquake 之后，而原文救援发生在倒塌的工厂现场、不是泛
泛震后救援，且漏掉了 factory 这个核心对象，覆盖不全。
借用原文：search teams were striving to ensure that no one is hurt further in the rescue operation
C) 偷换概念
A factory building being damaged in the earthquake. 用了 factory building 和
earthquake 两个原词，看着贴题。但它只讲『工厂被震损』这一点，既没涵盖占大半篇幅
的救援，也把成因（地震）当成了报道核心，仍是以偏概全。
借用原文：may have suffered damage in last week's earthquake

questions.stem: What are the products of this factory?

explain.定位:
It is not known what caused the collapse of the factory where plastic bags were manufactured.
工厂倒塌的原因尚不清楚，这家工厂是生产塑料袋的。
explain.信号:
定语从句 where…were manufactured 直接交代产品。答案句信号是 the factory where
plastic bags were manufactured 里的定语从句 where…were manufactured（生产……
的工厂），manufactured 一词正面回答『工厂生产什么』，听到
manufactured/produced 这类『生产』动词就锁定其宾语。
explain.替换:
plastic bags were manufactured ↔ Plastic bags.
录音 plastic bags 与选项原词一致，被动句改名词短语
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
Concrete and bricks. 直接抄录音里的 concrete and bricks，听到原词极易误选。但那是
救援人员翻找幸存者所穿过的废墟，是现场的瓦砾、不是工厂的产品，答非所问。
借用原文：picking through concrete and bricks to find survivors
B) 原词陷阱
Heavy machines. 借了录音里的 heavy machinery，但原文那是搜救队为救人而动用的重
型机械，属救援设备，不是这家工厂生产的东西，与 products 不符。
借用原文：with heavy machinery being used, search teams were striving
D) 偷换概念
Building materials. 没有原词，但它是对录音里 concrete and bricks 的上位概括（建筑材
料），引诱考生把废墟当成产品。原文从未说工厂生产建筑材料，只说生产 plastic bags，
故排除。
借用原文：picking through concrete and bricks to find survivors

questions.stem: What does iPhone SE share in common with iPhone 5 and 5s?

explain.定位:
It is the same size as the iPhone 5 and 5s.
它（iPhone SE）和 iPhone 5 与 5s 是同样的尺寸。
explain.信号:
the same … as 直陈『相同』。答案句的信号是表示『相同』的固定结构 the same size
as the iPhone 5 and 5s——题目问『共同点（share in common）』，录音里只要出现
the same … as（一样的……）这种把两者划等号的说法，那一句就是答案句。
explain.替换:
the same size as the iPhone 5 and 5s ↔ Its size.
把整句『同样尺寸』压缩成属性名 size
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
录音确实念到了颜色 the new model adds a color choice: rose gold，但用的是 adds
（新增）——玫瑰金是 SE 多出来的新颜色，是它和 5/5s 的『不同点』，正好与题目问的
『共同点』相反。听到 color 就选 A，是被原词钓走了。
借用原文：the new model adds a color choice: rose gold
B) 原词陷阱
录音说 the SE includes the better hardware of the most recent iPhone, the 6s——SE
的硬件来自最新的 6s，是更好的硬件，并非和 5/5s 相同。题目问的是与 5/5s 的共同点，
硬件恰恰不是。听到 hardware 这个原词就选，就中了原词陷阱。
借用原文：the SE includes the better hardware of the most recent iPhone, the 6s
C) 原词陷阱
录音说 Apple is offering the iPhone SE for a lower price——SE 价格是『更低』的，这
是与旧款的差别、是卖点，而非与 5/5s 的共同点。听到 price/dollars 一串就选 C，是被价
格信息引偏了。
借用原文：Apple is offering the iPhone SE for a lower price

questions.stem: How much will an iPhone SE with 64 GB of storage cost?

explain.定位:
An iPhone SE with 16 GB of storage will cost around $400. One with 64 GB will be about
$100 more.
16GB 存储的 iPhone SE 售价约 400 美元。64GB 的那款则要再贵约 100 美元。
explain.信号:
『$100 more』提示要在基准价上加。答案信号是加价说法 about $100 more——录音先
给 16GB 的基准价 cost around $400，再说 64GB 的 $100 more（再多 100）。看到/听
到 more、again、plus 这类词就知道：问的那个数要自己算，不是直接念出来的。
explain.替换:
will cost around $400 ↔ About 500 dollars.
基准价加上加价得总价
about $100 more ↔ About 500 dollars.
more=在基准上再加
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音里 An iPhone SE with 16 GB of storage will cost around $400——400 是 16GB 那
一档的价钱，可题目问的是 64GB。听到 $400 这个原数就选，是没分清问的是哪个配置。
借用原文：An iPhone SE with 16 GB of storage will cost around $400
D) 原词陷阱
录音 about $100 more 里的 100 是 64GB 比 16GB 多出来的『差价』，不是 64GB 的总
价。把差价当总价、直接选 100，就漏掉了 400 这个基准。
借用原文：about $100 more
C) 未提及
300 这个数在录音里从未出现，既不是任何配置的价，也不是差价，纯属凑出来的金额干扰
项，可直接排除。

questions.stem: What is the experimental therapy against blood cancer?

explain.定位:
An experimental therapy uses a person's weak immune system to fight deadly blood cancers.
一种实验性疗法利用人体虚弱的免疫系统来对抗致命的血液癌症。
explain.信号:
开篇定义句。新闻第一句往往直接点出报道主体，这句 An experimental therapy uses a
person's weak immune system to fight deadly blood cancers. 用"uses ... immune
system"为这项疗法定性——开篇定义即答案信号。
explain.替换:
uses a person's weak immune system to fight deadly blood cancers ↔
The immune system treatment.
动词描述改名词短语
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
录音确实念到 repetitive cycles of chemotherapy，但原文是说这新疗法"不需要"反复化
疗，The repeated chemotherapy. 正好把被否定的东西当成了答案，属听到
chemotherapy 就勾的反向陷阱。
借用原文：It doesn't require repeated treatments or repetitive cycles of chemotherapy
C) 原词陷阱
录音里 stem cell transplants 出现在说"这些患者此前各种常规疗法都失败了"的语境，是被
对比/排除的旧疗法，并非这项新疗法本身；The stem cell transplant. 把听到的原词直接
当答案。
借用原文：including many kinds of bone marrow and stem cell transplants
D) 原词陷阱
The bone marrow transplant. 与 C 同坑：bone marrow transplant 在原文里也属"患者
已经失败的常规疗法"之一，是被对照的旧法，不是这项实验疗法。
借用原文：including many kinds of bone marrow and stem cell transplants

questions.stem: How many patients gained a complete remission in the small trials?

explain.定位:
In one study of 35 patients with a type of leukemia, 94 percent experienced a
complete remission.
在一项针对 35 名某型白血病患者的研究中，94% 的人实现了完全缓解。
explain.信号:
complete remission 同词锁定。题干问 complete remission，录音里 94 percent
experienced a complete remission 出现同一短语，这句即答案句；而真正要的人数藏
在"35 人的 94%"里，须由两数相乘得出。
explain.替换:
In one study of 35 patients with a type of leukemia, 94 percent experienced a complete remission ↔
About 33.
35 的 94% 约等于 33
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
35 patients 确被念到，但它是"研究纳入的总人数"，题目问的是"完全缓解的人数"。About

questions.stem: What have Hutchinson researchers contributed to according to the news report?
options: A) Improving cancer-fighting ability of immune cells.
B) Encouraging patients with skin or lung cancers.
C) Healing the leukemia patients in a single treatment.
D) Eradicating invading viruses and bacteria.

explain.定位:
The work by Hutchinson researchers increases this natural cancer-fighting ability.
Hutchinson 研究者的工作增强了这种天然的抗癌能力。
explain.信号:
主体作主语的成果句。这句 The work by Hutchinson researchers increases this natural
cancer-fighting ability. 正以研究者的工作为主语、动词 increases 点出贡献——主体 + 动
作的成果句，就是答案信号；其中 this 指代前句免疫细胞的抗癌力。
explain.替换:
increases this natural cancer-fighting ability ↔
Improving cancer-fighting ability of immune cells.
increases 同义 improving
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音末句 shown promise against skin cancer and some lung cancers 确有 skin/lung
cancers，但说的是"该免疫疗法对皮肤癌肺癌也显出前景"，不是"鼓励患者"。Encouraging
patients with skin or lung cancers. 把原词拼到了一个原文没说的动作上。
借用原文：Using the immune system has also shown promise against skin cancer and some
lung cancers
C) 过度推断
录音里 it's a single treatment 和 leukemia 都念到了，但原文只说"单次治疗"且 94% 缓
解，并未说"一次就治愈所有白血病患者"。Healing the leukemia patients in a single
treatment. 把"缓解"夸成"治愈"、说得比原文绝对。
借用原文：it's a single treatment instead of many months of treatment
D) 张冠李戴
录音 Immune system cells usually fight invading viruses and bacteria 里的
viruses/bacteria 描述的是免疫细胞"通常"的功能，并非 Hutchinson 研究者的贡献。
Eradicating invading viruses and bacteria. 把别人/常态的事安到研究者头上。
借用原文：Immune system cells usually fight invading viruses and bacteria

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's company?
options: A) It specializes in safety from leaks.
B) It is headquartered in London.
C) It has a chemical processing plant.
D) It has a partnership with LCP.

explain.定位:
Well, I understand that your company has a chemical processing plant.
嗯，我了解到贵公司有一座化工厂（化学处理工厂）。
explain.信号:
I understand引出已知事实。男方用 I understand that your company has a chemical
processing plant 把"对方公司的情况"作为已知前提抛出，I understand that… 正是引
出"关于该公司的事实"的信号句，答案就在这句里。
explain.替换:
your company has a chemical processing plant ↔ It has a chemical processing plant
your company换成It
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
It specializes in safety from leaks. 盗用了男方介绍自己公司时说的 is a leader in safety
from leaks——但"擅长防泄漏"是男方 LCP 的业务，不是女方公司的，题目问的是 the
woman's company，张冠李戴。
借用原文：LCP, Liquid Control Products, is a leader in safety from leaks
B) 原词陷阱
It is headquartered in London. 里的 London 来自男方 calling from London——伦敦是
打电话进来的男方所在地，不是女方公司总部所在地，听到 London 就选是被原词诱导。
借用原文：calling from London
D) 过度推断
It has a partnership with LCP. 用了原文反复出现的 LCP，但全程男方只是打电话来"想谈
合作"（discuss ways in which we could help TGC），双方根本还没建立 partnership，
属过度推断。
借用原文：discuss ways in which we could help TGC protect itself from such problems

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man?
options: A) He is a safety inspector.
B) He is Mr. Grand's friend.

explain.定位:
My own company, LCP, Liquid Control Products, is a leader in safety from leaks in the field
of chemical processing. I'd like to speak to Mr. Grand to discuss ways in which we could help
TGC protect itself from such problems and save money at the same time.
我自己的公司 LCP（液体控制产品公司）是化工处理领域防泄漏方面的领先者。我想和
Grand 先生谈谈，看我们能怎样帮 TGC 防范这类问题，同时还能省钱。
explain.信号:
推销话术暴露身份。他主动夸自家公司 is a leader in safety from leaks、想约人谈 help
TGC protect itself from such problems and save money——这套"夸产品＋帮你省钱＋
约见面"的话术是销售员的典型动作，正是判断身份的信号。
explain.替换:
we could help TGC protect itself from such problems and save money ↔ He is a salesman
推销行为概括为身份
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
He is a safety inspector. 借了原文的 safety（safety from leaks）——但 safety 是他卖的
产品方向，他是来推销的，不是来检查 TGC 安全的，安全检查员属凭原词臆造的身份。
借用原文：is a leader in safety from leaks
B) 未提及
He is Mr. Grand's friend. 在录音里毫无依据——他是陌生来电，连本人都没找到，女士还
要他寄资料、提供推荐信，显然不是 Grand 的朋友，属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱
He is a chemist. 靠 chemical processing 里的 chemical 来骗——chemical 是描述行业
领域的，不代表他本人是化学家，他做的是销售而非搞化学研究，读音相近的偷换。
借用原文：in the field of chemical processing

questions.stem: What is the woman's position in her company?
options: B) Head of the personnel department.
D) Director of the safety department.

explain.定位:
You're speaking to his personal assistant. I can deal with calls for Mr. Grand.
您正在跟他的私人助理通话。我可以处理找 Grand 先生的来电。
explain.信号:
被问后的直接自报。男方追问能否找别人（Could I speak to someone else），女方紧接
着应答 You're speaking to his personal assistant——这是被问之后的直接自报身份句，
对话题答案就落在这种应答上。
explain.替换:
You're speaking to his personal assistant ↔ Mr. Grand's personal assistant
his还原为Mr. Grand's
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
The public relations officer. 在录音里根本没出现，纯属"接电话的人想当然是公关"的常识
臆断，原文女方自报的是 personal assistant，未提及公关。
B) 未提及
Head of the personnel department. 录音通篇未提人事部门，女方明确说自己是私人助
理，此项为无中生有。
D) 原词陷阱
Director of the safety department. 里的 safety 来自男方介绍业务时的 safety from
leaks——那是男方公司的业务方向，与女方职位无关，是把别处的热词拼成一个假职位。
借用原文：safety from leaks in the field of chemical processing

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do?
options: A) Send a comprehensive description of their work.
B) Provide details of their products and services.
C) Leave a message for Mr. Grand.
D) Wait for Mr. Grand to call back.

explain.定位:
Listen, let me suggest something. You send us details of your products and services, together
with references from other companies. And then we'll contact you.
这样吧，我给您出个主意。您把贵公司产品和服务的详细资料、连同其他公司的推荐信一起
寄给我们，然后我们再联系您。
explain.信号:
let me suggest引出建议。女方用 let me suggest something 明确引出建议，紧接着的
You send us details of your products and services 就是她要男方做的事——"建议某人
做某事"的答案信号就是这种提议句。
explain.替换:
You send us details of your products and services ↔
Provide details of their products and services
send改provide、人称转换
explain.排除:
A) 偷换概念
Send a comprehensive description of their work. 用了和正确项一样的 Send／
description 套路，但女方要的是 details of your products and services（产品和服务的
资料），不是"对他们工作的全面描述"，把"产品服务"偷换成了"工作"。
借用原文：details of your products and services, together with references from other companies
C) 未提及
Leave a message for Mr. Grand. 是打电话场景的"想当然"动作，但女方从头到尾没让男方
留言，而是让他寄资料，属用常识替原文、未提及。
D) 与原文相反
Wait for Mr. Grand to call back. 弄反了联系方向：原文是男方寄资料后 we'll contact
you（公司联系男方），而非男方坐等 Mr. Grand 本人回电，且回电主体也错。
借用原文：And then we'll contact you

questions.stem: What do we know about the woman before she went to Europe?
options: A) She listened to recordings of many European orchestras.
B) She read a lot about European musicians and their music.
C) She dreamed of working and living in a European country.
D) She learned playing the violin from a famous French musician.

explain.定位:
No, not really, although I've always listened to recordings of great orchestras from Europe.
不，其实没有，不过我一直都在听欧洲那些伟大乐团的录音。
explain.信号:
转折 although 后才是真意。她先说 No, not really（没怎么想过），紧接 although 一
转，后半 I've always listened to recordings of great orchestras from Europe 才是她真
正做过的事——转折连词后面那句才是答案落点。
explain.替换:
listened to recordings of great orchestras from Europe ↔
listened to recordings of many European orchestras
great→many、from Europe→European 的同义改写
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
录音只说她"听"乐团录音 listened to recordings，从没说她"读"了很多关于音乐家的书，
read a lot about European musicians 是把"听"换成了"读"，属未提及的动作。
C) 与原文相反
录音里男声问她是否想过 P2… 但她答 No, not really，明确说没怎么想过住在西方/欧洲；
dreamed of working and living in a European country 借了"European"却把她否定掉的
事说成她梦想过，与原文相反。
借用原文：No, not really
D) 未提及
录音从没说她师从任何法国音乐家，她只说 I began violin lessons at school（在学校学
的）；learned playing the violin from a famous French musician 里的"法国名家"是无
中生有，"French"是顺着后文巴黎联想硬造的。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her music experience?
options: A) She was a pupil of a famous European violinist.
B) She gave her first performance with her father.
C) She became a professional violinist at fifteen.
D) She began taking violin lessons as a small child.

explain.定位:
Yes, I began violin lessons at school when I was 6.
是的，我6岁就在学校开始上小提琴课了。
explain.信号:
被问者对"早学"的直接应答。男声问 You were born in 1955 并由前文"很小就喜欢古典
乐"引出，她直接应答 I began violin lessons at school when I was 6，"6 岁开始学"这一
被问者的直接交代就是答案句。
explain.替换:
I began violin lessons ↔ began taking violin lessons
began…lessons 近乎原样，仅补 taking
when I was 6 ↔ as a small child
具体年龄 6 概括成 small child
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
录音说她在学校开始学 violin lessons at school，没有任何"师从某欧洲名小提琴家"的情
节；a pupil of a famous European violinist 借了"violin/violinist"造出一个"名师"，属未
提及。
B) 张冠李戴
录音里父亲只是 my father had bought me a new violin（给她买了把新琴），首演是她 I

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about William Shakespeare?
options: A) There are mysterious stories behind his works.
B) His personal history is little known.
C) His works have no match worldwide.
D) There are many misunderstandings about him.

explain.定位:
Yet how many know Shakespeare, the person, the man behind the works? After centuries of
research, scholars are still trying to discover Shakespeare's personal history. It is not easily
found in his writings.
然而又有多少人了解作品背后的莎士比亚这个人呢？经过数百年的研究，学者们仍在努力发
掘莎士比亚的个人经历。它在他的作品里并不容易找到。
explain.信号:
转折词 Yet 之后转入真正主旨。前文铺垫"大家熟悉他的作品"，Yet how many know
Shakespeare, the person 一个 Yet 把焦点扭向"这个人本身"，转折后才是 speaker 真正要
谈的点；再接 scholars are still trying to discover Shakespeare's personal history，坐
实主旨是"其生平至今难以查清"。
explain.替换:
scholars are still trying to discover Shakespeare's personal history ↔
His personal history is little known.
"还在努力发掘"="鲜为人知"
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音开头确有 What makes a person famous? This is a mystery 和 the works，A 把
mystery 和 works 拼成"作品背后有神秘故事"，听到原词很想选；但原文的 mystery 指"成
名之谜/生平之谜"，并非"作品背后有神秘故事"，答非所问。
借用原文：This is a mystery that many people have carefully thought about
C) 过度推断
原文说他是 one of the greatest English writers，C 顺势说"his works have no match
worldwide（举世无双）"，听到 greatest 很想选；但原文只说"最伟大作家之一"，是 one
of，没说无人能及，C 把程度推过头了。
借用原文：one of the greatest English writers of the 16th and 17th centuries
D) 偷换概念
原文确实说 Many myths arose about Shakespeare，D 借"myths"说成"许多误解"很像；
但全段主旨是"生平不为人知"，myths（流传的传说）只是其中一个支撑细节，不是
speaker 关于他要表达的"主要"内容，以偏概全。
借用原文：Many myths arose about Shakespeare

questions.stem: What do we learn about Shakespeare's father?
options: A) He once worked in a well-known acting company.
B) He moved to Stratford-on-Avon in his childhood.
C) He failed to go beyond grammar school.
D) He was a member of the town council.

explain.定位:
Shakespeare's father was a respected man in Stratford-upon-Avon, a member of the
town council.
莎士比亚的父亲是斯特拉福镇上一位受人尊敬的人，是镇议会的成员。
explain.信号:
主语直接出现"father"，应答题干对象。题干问父亲，原文 Shakespeare's father was a
respected man 主语正是 father，紧跟其后的同位语 a member of the town council 直
接交代其身份，是回答本题对象的那一句。
explain.替换:
a member of the town council ↔ He was a member of the town council.
近乎原句对应，只是补出主语 He
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 An acting company, for example, could change a play 出现过 acting
company，A 借它说"他曾在知名剧团工作"，听到原词很想选；但原文那句讲的是"剧团可
随意改剧本"，根本没说父亲（或莎翁）在剧团工作过，纯属把原词挪作他用。
借用原文：An acting company, for example, could change a play if they wanted to
B) 未提及
原文 Stratford-upon-Avon 是讲父亲所在的镇，B 却说"他童年时搬到斯特拉福"，既偷换
了对象（题干问父亲），又凭空加了"童年迁居"这一原文没有的动作，地名是真的、事却是
编的。
借用原文：Shakespeare's father was a respected man in Stratford-upon-Avon

原文 He sent young William to grammar school 说父亲把莎翁送进文法学校、且
Shakespeare did have at least an average education，C 却说"他没读过文法学校以
上"，把"读了书"反成"没读上去"，方向相反；况且本题问的是父亲，C 说的是 William。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say parts of Shakespeare's life will remain a mystery?
options: A) People of his time had little interest in him.
B) His works were adapted beyond recognition.
C) Possible sources of clues about him were lost in a fire.
D) Writers of his time had no means to protect their works.

Some parts of Shakespeare's life will always remain unknown. The Great London Fire of
1666 burned many important documents that could've been a source of clues.
莎士比亚生平的某些部分将永远不为人知。1666 年的伦敦大火烧毁了许多本可作为线索来
源的重要文献。

结果句后紧跟的因果陈述句。先抛结果 Some parts of Shakespeare's life will always
remain unknown，紧接 The Great London Fire of 1666 burned many important
documents that could've been a source of clues 给出原因——大火烧掉了本可作线索的
文献，这句正是 Why 的答案。
explain.替换:
The Great London Fire of 1666 burned many important documents that could've been a source of
clues
↔ Possible sources of clues about him were lost in a fire.
"大火烧毁文献"="线索来源毁于火灾"
explain.排除:
A) 未提及

B) 过度推断
原文 An acting company… could change a play 说剧团可改剧本，B 借它说"作品被改得
面目全非"，听到 change 很想选；但那句是解释"作者作品难留下"的旁证，且 change a
play 远不到"beyond recognition（面目全非）"的程度，既非本题原因又把程度推过头。

questions.stem: What is mentioned as a most common danger when people go travelling abroad?

While the majority of people you meet when travelling are sure to be friendly and welcoming,

questions.stem: What is the most important thing to do when you prepare for your trip abroad?
options: C) Book tickets well in advance.

explain.定位:
As you prepare for your trip, make sure you have the right paperwork. You don't want to get
to your destination, only to find you have the wrong visa, or worse, that your passport isn't
valid anymore.
在你准备出行时，务必确保你备齐了正确的文件。你可不想到了目的地才发现签证办错了，
或者更糟，护照已经失效。

建议句 make sure 领起第一项准备。答案句以 As you prepare for your trip, make sure
you have the right paperwork 领起准备清单，用 make sure（务必）这一强调式建议把
『备齐正确文件』摆在第一位，后面又用签证作废、护照失效这类后果加重它的分量——
make sure 加首位加后果强调，就是这题的答案信号。

make sure you have the right paperwork ↔ Have the right documents.

Book tickets well in advance.（提前订票）原文第二段只说 prepare for your trip in
advance（提前做准备），并没说提前订票；这里盗用了听感相近的 in advance，让人误以

Always go to bus and taxi stands. ↔ Use official transport.

Contact your agent.（联系你的代理/旅行社）原文到达段（第三段）只讲了用官方交通、

Get a lift if possible.（尽量搭便车）盗用了原文真念到的 lift：原文却是 Don't accept

questions.stem: What did Gerald Ratner decide to do when he took over his father's shops?
options: B) Refine the taste of his goods.

questions.stem: On what occasion did Gerald Ratner explain the secret of his success?
options: A) At a meeting of top British businesspeople.
B) During a local sales promotion campaign.
C) During a live television interview.

At a big meeting of top British business people, he showed up and explained the secret of

句首地点状语。录音把场合放在句首作状语 At a big meeting of top British business

At a big meeting of top British business people ↔ At a meeting of top British businesspeople

questions.stem: How did people feel when they learned of Gerald Ratner's remarks?

People felt insulted and stayed away from Ratner's shops.

People felt insulted ↔ Insulted

options: A) He is not laughed at, that laughs at himself first.
B) There should be a limit to one's sense of humour.
C) He who never learns from the past is bound to fail.
D) The words of some businesspeople are just rubbish.

英国人素以善于自嘲闻名，但即便他们的幽默感也有限度——零售商 Gerald Ratner 就为此
付出了惨痛代价。

Reaping the Rewards of Risk-Taking

A) Since Steve Jobs resigned as chief executive of Apple, much has been said about him as a peerless business leader who has created immense wealth for shareholders, and guided the design of hit products that are transforming entire industries, like music and mobile communications.

B) All true, but let's think different, to borrow the Apple marketing slogan of years back. Let's look at Mr. Jobs as a role model.

C) Above all, he is an innovator(创新者). His creative force is seen in products such as the iPod, iPhone, and iPad, and in new business models for pricing and distributing music and mobile software online. Studies of innovation come to the same conclusion: you can't engineer innovation, but you can increase the odds of it occurring. And Mr. Jobs' career can be viewed as a consistent pursuit of improving those odds, both for himself and the companies he has led. Mr. Jobs, of course, has enjoyed singular success. But innovation, broadly defined, is the crucial ingredient in all economic progress—higher growth for nations, more competitive products for companies, and more prosperous careers for individuals. And Mr. Jobs, many experts say, exemplifies what works in the innovation game.

D) "We can look at and learn from Steve Jobs what the essence of American innovation is," says John Kao, an innovation consultant to corporations and governments. "Many other nations," Mr. John Kao notes, "are now ahead of the United States in producing what are considered the raw materials of innovation. These include government financing for scientific research, national policies to support emerging industries, educational achievement, engineers and scientists graduated, even the speeds of Internet broadband service."

E) Yet what other nations typically lack, Mr. Kao adds, is a social environment that encourages diversity, experimentation, risk-taking, and combining skills from many fields into products that he calls "recombinant mash-ups(打碎重组)," like the iPhone, which redefined the smartphone category. "The culture of other countries doesn't support the kind of innovation that Steve Jobs exemplifies, as America does," Mr. John Kao says.

F) Workers of every rank are told these days that wide-ranging curiosity and continuous learning are vital to thriving in the modern economy. Formal education matters, career counselors say, but real-life experience is often even more valuable.

G) An adopted child, growing up in Silicon Valley, Mr. Jobs displayed those traits early on. He was fascinated by electronics as a child, building Heath kit do-it-yourself projects, like radios. Mr. Jobs dropped out of Reed College after only a semester and traveled around India in search of spiritual enlightenment, before returning to Silicon Valley to found Apple with his friend, Stephen Wozniak, an engineering wizard(奇才). Mr. Jobs was forced out of Apple in 1985, went off and founded two other companies, Next and Pixar, before returning to Apple in 1996 and becoming chief executive in 1997.

H) His path was unique, but innovation experts say the pattern of exploration is not unusual. "It's often people like Steve Jobs who can draw from a deep reservoir of diverse experiences that often generate breakthrough ideas and insights," says Hal Gregersen, a professor at the European Institute of Business Administration.

I) Mr. Gregersen is a co-author of a new book, "The Innovator's DNA," which is based on an eight-year study of 5000(创业者) and executives worldwide. His two collaborators and co-authors are Jeff Dyer, a professor at Brigham Young University, and Clayton Christensen, a professor at the Harvard Business School, whose 1997 book "The Innovator's Dilemma" popularized the concept of disruptive(颠覆性的) innovation.

J) The academics identify five traits that are common to the disruptive innovators: questioning, experimenting, observing, associating and networking. Their bundle of characteristics echoes the ceaseless curiosity and willingness to take risks noted by other experts. Networking, Mr. Hal Gregersen explains, is less about career-building relationships than a consistent search for new ideas. Associating, he adds, is the ability to make idea-producing connections by linking concepts from different disciplines.

K) "Innovators engage in these mental activities regularly," Mr. Gregersen says. "It's a habit for them." Innovative companies, according to the authors, typically enjoy higher valuations in the stock market, which they call an "innovation premium(溢价)." It is calculated by estimating the share of a company's value that cannot be accounted for by its current products and cash flow. The innovation premium tries to quantify(量化) investors' bets that a company will do even better in the future because of innovation.

L) Apple, by their calculations, had a 37 percent innovation premium during Mr. Jobs' first term with the company. His years in exile resulted in a 31 percent innovation discount. After his return, Apple fortunes improved gradually at first, and improved markedly starting in 2005, yielding a 52 percent innovation premium since then.

M) There is no conclusive proof, but Mr. Hal Gregersen says it is unlikely that Mr. Jobs could have reshaped industries beyond computing, as he has done in his second term at Apple, without the experience outside the company, especially at Pixar—the computer-animation(动画制作) studio that created a string of critically and commercially successful movies, such as "Toy Story" and "Up."

N) Mr. Jobs suggested much the same thing during a commencement address to the graduating class at Stanford University in 2005. "It turned out that getting fired from Apple was the best thing that could have ever happened to me," he told the students. Mr. Jobs also spoke of perseverance(坚持) and will power. "Sometimes life hits you in the head with a brick," he said. "Don't lose faith." Mark D. Shermis, a professor at the University of Akron in Ohio, supervised the Hewlett Foundation's contest on automated essay scoring and wrote a paper about the experiment. In his view, the technology—though imperfect—has a place in educational settings.

O) Mr. Jobs ended his commencement talk with a call to innovation, both in one's choice of work and in one's life. Be curious, experiment, take risks, he said to the students. His advice was emphasized by the words on the back of the final edition of The Whole Earth Catalog, which he quoted, "Stay hungry. Stay foolish." And, Mr. Jobs said, "I have always wished that for myself. And now, as you graduate to begin anew, I wish that for you." "There seems to be a lack of appreciation of what is actually going on in the real world."

questions.stem: What does the author try to draw attention to?
options: A) Food riots and hunger in the world.
B) News headlines in the leading media.
C) The decline of the grain yield growth.
D) The food supply in populous countries.
questions.passage:
Some of the world's most significant problems never hit headlines. One example comes from agriculture. Food riots and hunger make news. But the trend lying behind these matters is rarely talked about. This is the decline in the growth in yields of some of the world's major crops. A new study by the University of Minnesota and McGill University in Montreal looks at where, and how far, this decline is occurring.

The authors take a vast number of data points for the four most important crops: rice, wheat, corn and soybeans(大豆). They find that in between 24% and 39% of all harvested areas, the improvement in yields that took place before the 1980s slowed down in the 1990s and 2000s.

There are two worrying features of the slowdown. One is that it has been particularly sharp in the world's most populous(人口多的) countries, India and China. Their ability to feed themselves has been an important source of relative stability both within the countries and on world food markets. That self-sufficiency cannot be taken for granted if yields continue to slow down or reverse.

Second, yield growth has been lower in wheat and rice than in corn and soybeans. This is problematic because wheat and rice are more important as foods, accounting for around half of all calories consumed. Corn and soybeans are more important as feed grains. The authors note that "we have preferentially focused our crop improvement efforts on feeding animals and cars rather than on crops that feed people and are the basis of food security in much of the world."

The report qualifies the more optimistic findings of another new paper which suggests that the world will not have to dig up a lot more land for farming in order to feed 9 billion people in 2050, as the Food and Agriculture Organisation has argued.

Instead, it says, thanks to slowing population growth, land currently ploughed up for crops might be able to revert(回返) to forest or wilderness. This could happen. The trouble is that the forecast assumes continued improvements in yields, which may not actually happen.

options: A) More men taking an extended parental leave.
B) People's changing attitudes towards family.
C) More women entering business management.

questions.passage:
The endless debate about "work-life balance" often contains a hopeful footnote about stay-at-home dads. If American society and business won't make it easier on future female leaders who choose to have children, there is still the ray of hope that increasing numbers of full-time fathers will. But based on today's socioeconomic trends, this hope is, unfortunately, misguided.

It's true that the number of men who have left work to do their thing as full-time parents has doubled in a decade, but it's still very small: only 0.8% of married couples where the stay-at-home father was out of the labor force for a year. Even that percentage is likely inflated by men thrust into their caretaker role by a downsizing. This is simply not a large enough group to reduce the social stigma(污名) and force other adjustments necessary to supporting men in this decision, even if only for a relatively short time.

Even shorter times away from work for working fathers are already difficult. A study found that 85% of new fathers take some time off after the birth of a child—but for all but a few, it's a week or two at most. Meanwhile, the average for women who take leave is more than 10 weeks.
